subject: Inconsistant pvalue in parameterEstimates and standardizedSolutions

messages.author: 1ff876476824ff7e
messages.subject: Inconsistant pvalue in parameterEstimates and standardizedSolutions
parts:
Hi, 
I noticed a discrepancy between the p values from the parameterEstimates() function and the standardizedSolutions() function. For example:

example(cfa)
fit_sol1 <- parameterEstimates(fit, standardized = T)
fit_sol2 <- standardizedSolution(fit)

solution_compare <- left_join(fit_sol1 %>% select(lhs, op,rhs,std.all,se,z,pvalue), fit_sol2 %>% select(lhs, op,rhs,est.std,se,z,pvalue), by = c("lhs","op","rhs"),, suffix = c(".PE", ".SS"))

This is what I get:
My question is why are these different? And if I want to fully standardized parameter estimates (estimate, se and pvalue), which should I report?

messages.author: 5b9c62b1c7cbc1e6
messages.subject: Re: Inconsistant pvalue in parameterEstimates and standardizedSolutions
parts:
Rebekka,

This comes up now and again. It applies to regression in general, not just SEM or lavaan.

The parameter estimate is a single estimate with uncertainty.

The standardized parameter estimate transforms that with a calculation that uses two other estimates (the variances), each with their own uncertainty.

So you shouldn't expect the p-values to be the same. Always draw conclusions based on the unstandardized estimate and its tests/CIs. Standardized estimates are nothing more than a convenience for interpretation.

Pat
